title: Romania's record recycled table raises funds for children's hospital
summary:
A community meal in Romania needed a remarkably long table: 3.1 miles, or 4.99 kilometers. About 20,000 people gathered at the Uniting Table in Bucharest on September 12, 2026.

The table set a Guinness World Record for the longest table made from recycled materials. Recycling means processing used materials so they can serve another purpose. In this case, those materials became a place for thousands of people to share a meal.

The organizer, nonprofit Bloom The World, had another goal alongside the record. The event raised more than $110,000 for Romania's first psychiatric hospital for children. A psychiatric hospital provides specialist care for mental health and related needs. The planned hospital will care for children with conditions including depression, autism and ADHD.

Children in Bucharest who need mental health care are currently treated in an outdated facility. Its large, crowded wards lack basic privacy. The new hospital is scheduled to open in 2027.

This was Bloom's second record of this kind. In 2025, the organization brought together 10,000 people around a table made from recycled materials in Alba Iulia, Romania. That table measured 1.7 miles, or 2.7 kilometers. The earlier event focused on bringing people together and raising awareness of environmental issues.

Bloom intends to recycle the latest table's materials again to make children's furniture. After providing a shared dining space, the materials have another planned purpose.
why_it_matters: The event combined a community gathering with fundraising for a planned children's hospital. It also connected the use of recycled materials with a further planned use as children's furniture.
